sources.note: Relation millénaire and Relations actuelles: family territories, seasonal work and continuing relationships with land. Archaeological occupation does not establish a state founding.

sources.note: Lake gatherings, colonial displacement and purchase chronology. The specific 1956 land sale and 1958 reserve recognition are distinguished from broader founding labels.

sources.note: Plaque and Heritage Value, long occupation and trading posts. Conflicting designation dates on the page are not repeated.

sources.title: Canadian Journal of Archaeology, Iroquoian Pottery at Lake Abitibi, 2009
sources.note: Public abstract, volume 33(1), pages 65 to 91. The restricted article was not read; vessel style is not treated as proof of population replacement.

sources.title: Chloe Lee-Hone, Entre le Saguenay et la Huronie, 2019
sources.note: Université de Montréal thesis repository abstract: Bérubé, Margot and Louis collections, typological dating and exchange interpretation. The full thesis was not read.

sources.title: Conseil de la Première Nation Abitibiwinni, Langue et culture Anicinape
sources.note: Nigamou, the Minawasi mural and vocabulary placemats. Educational aims are distinguished from measured learning outcomes.

sources.title: Conseil de la Première Nation Abitibiwinni, Artisanat et artistes peintres
sources.note: Harry Wylde biography, teaching and painting technique; no undated activity is given an invented year.

sources.title: Première Nation Abitibiwinni, Projets
sources.note: Territory interviews beginning in 2015 and environmental DNA collaboration with INRS. Broken counters and unconfirmed wildlife detections are excluded.

sources.title: Première Nation Abitibiwinni, ATIK, le caribou
sources.note: Detour Kesagami collaboration, 2022 joint inventory and ATIK forum. Conservation activity is not evidence that populations have recovered.
